name: Check Position
description: Simple daily Google position tracking across multiple datacenters. Pricing (company-stated): 7 keywords free, €15/month or €162/year. Listed for sale at $20,000 (2.8×), with 18 offers and 2,145 interested-buyer views (TrustMRR).

mentions.evidence: ~$1,807 MRR, 235 active subscriptions, 60% L30 margin (snapshot), ~$601 L30 (−46%; annual renewals are lumpy), ~$38,277 last 12 months, ~$209,829 all-time. The trend is downward (L6M $13.5k vs L12M $38.3k), which is probably why it is for sale. Revenue synced Oct 14, 2026 ~04:43 Warsaw.
mentions.indieAngle: A cheap acquisition target. About $38k a year verified against a $20k ask, if the decline can be stopped with SERP-API cost control and annual-plan pushes.

whyItPrints: Rank tracking is a commodity and SEO people still pay for a cheap one. 235 subscribers on cheap plans add up to a long tail.
whyThisMatters:
It checks where a site ranks on Google, across several datacenters, and keeps the history. You can import keywords, open the results page, compare two dates, and watch whether specific URLs are indexed. A paid plan unlocks an API that can create and delete those checks from your own tools, with Slack help for the integration. A handful of keywords is free. The pack on the site is a few hundred keywords for a low monthly price, or a cheaper annual payment, with a daily refresh and a limited number of instant seven-datacenter checks.

The listing is for sale. The last 30 days are much quieter than the last year. That can be annual renewals landing in a lump, and it can also be a product that has been shrinking, which is the note on the listing. The ask is a low multiple of the trailing year. Two thousand people have looked at the sale page.

You pay so a daily rank check does not require a bigger SEO suite.
